sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Plasma-membrane protrusion localisation confirmed by co-localisation with prominin-1; no functional assay reported. NOT MEASURED beyond surface localisation.
sites.rationale: PROM2 is a 5-TM protein whose N-terminus (residue 27 onward) is extracellular after cleavage of the 26-residue signal peptide, while the C-terminus (residue 834) is intracellular. Because exactly one terminus is extracellular, the topology_derived rule places the GFP fusion after residue 26 (the SP cleavage junction), giving residue_before=G (residue 26) and residue_after=A (residue 27). The junction is 77 residues from TM1 (residue 104), well clear of the ≥3-residue TM boundary constraint. Confidence is low because the paper does not state whether GFP is N- or C-terminal; the C-terminal (intracellular) possibility cannot be excluded from the text alone. PROM2 expressed as a GFP fusion chimera in CHO cells (PMID 12514187); the construct localises to plasma membrane protrusions and co-localises with prominin-1. No residue or terminus is named in the paper.

sources.claim: Although the amino acid identity between prominin-2 and prominin-1 is low (<30%), their genomic organization is strikingly similar, suggesting an early gene duplication event. Like prominin-1, prominin-2 exhibits a characteristic membrane topology with five transmembrane segments and two large glycosylated extracellular loops. Upon its ectopic expression in Chinese hamster ovary cells as a green fluorescent protein fusion chimera, prominin-2 was also found to be associated with plasma membrane protrusions, as revealed by its co-localization with prominin-1, suggesting a related role.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It reports a GFP fusion chimera of full-length PROM2 in CHO cells with plasma-membrane protrusion localisation but names neither the terminus nor any residue. The topology_derived rule is applied: PROM2 has exactly one extracellular terminus (N-terminus after SP cleavage at residue 26), yielding insert_after_residue=26. The C-terminal position (residue 834) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. Confidence is low throughout because the GFP terminus is not stated in the paper.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminus of PROM2 is intracellular (IC3, residues 801-834); if the GFP fusion reported in PMID 12514187 is C-terminal, it faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface tag site.
